name: Puppet Boss
summary: The Puppet Boss is a puppeteer-type encounter shown in the official 4K demo, and the first boss S-GAME put in front of the public. It fights with strings - controlling attacks from range while still delivering fast melee strikes up close - which makes it the clearest early demonstration of the game's mixed range design.
observed: Humanoid puppeteer silhouette
String-based ranged attacks
Swift close-range strikes between the ranged sets
Shown in the 4K demo, so the mechanics shown are from a build S-GAME chose to present publicly

name: Huangxing
summary: Huangxing is an aggressive warrior boss featured in the 4K demo footage, built around relentless melee pressure rather than ranged tools. The demo shows fast multi-hit sword combos and an unblockable grab, which is the combination that forces a player to dodge rather than turtle behind the Sha-chi block.
observed: Warrior-type, melee-focused
Fast multi-hit sword combos
An unblockable grab that has to be dodged, not blocked
Aggressive forward pressure with little downtime

name: Seven Stars
summary: Seven Stars is a named boss from promotional material, described as a multi-phase encounter. Beyond the name and the phase structure, nothing has been shown in enough detail to describe the fight honestly.
observed: Named in official promotional material
Multi-phase design indicated
No extended gameplay footage released

name: Lion Dance
summary: Lion Dance is a beast-type boss whose design is built on the Chinese lion dance tradition. It has appeared in trailer footage only, so its attack set is not yet describable.
observed: Beast-type boss
Design drawn from Chinese lion dance performance
Trailer appearance only

name: Drunken Sword
summary: Drunken Sword is a swordsman boss using unpredictable drunken-style sword techniques - a recognised martial arts form, and one whose whole point is that the rhythm does not read like a standard attack cadence.
observed: Swordsman-type boss
Drunken-style technique set
Unpredictable timing is the design intent
Trailer appearance only

name: Double Boss Fight
summary: A simultaneous two-boss encounter revealed in the August 2026 State of Play showcase. It is the only major new mechanic revealed at that broadcast, and the one that most changes how the fight system reads - everything about positioning, parry priority and target selection becomes a different problem with two health bars at once.
observed: Two bosses fought simultaneously
Revealed August 2026 at the State of Play deep dive
No individual boss names released for the pairing

name: Commander Cleave
source: Playable 2024 demo, covered by IGN hands-on
summary: Commander Cleave is the second boss available in Phantom Blade Zero's playable demo and the one that functions as the demo's real skill check. He is a larger opponent built around a cleaver sword that breaks through defensive play, and the hands-on coverage describes timing as the answer to him rather than aggression or blocking.
observed: Fought after the Tie Sha section of the demo
Wields a cleaver sword whose attacks tear through Soul's guard
Substantial health pool and its own defensive options
Described in coverage as the first genuine skill test the demo presents
tips: The cleaver attacks are the ones to read rather than block, which matters because blocking also spends the Sha-chi resource you need for your own heavy attacks
Weapon swapping is the practical tool here: switching restores stamina immediately, so a combo can be continued instead of abandoned when the health bar does not move

name: The Hunt
location: Appears in the opening, fighting Soul atop a moving wagon
source: IGN boss footage released 13 October 2026, described by GamingBolt and 7GrandSteps
summary: The Hunt is the assassin Soul fights on the moving cart during the game's opening, and the October 2026 footage shows him again as a full encounter rather than a scripted escape. He is built around relentless pressure rather than single heavy hits: coverage describes the danger as death by a hundred small cuts, which sounds punishing but is also what makes him readable, because his aggression keeps creating parry windows.
observed: Fights with a pair of one-handed axes joined by a chain, used for rapid strikes followed by disengaging withdrawals
A move that looks like an acrobatic backward somersault is the wind-up for throwing one of the axes
Second phase: he grows two additional arms, each carrying another axe, so the fight becomes four-axe coverage
His style is described as aggressive rather than tanky, with constant openings for a player who can read the chain attacks
What weapon or reward he grants has not been announced, despite store copy saying weapons are taken from fallen foes
tips: Everything here comes from preview footage, so treat it as expectation rather than strategy: the numbers, ranges and any guard-break timings are unknown until the full build is public
The somersault is the tell worth learning from the clip - if you read it as evasion you will whiff a parry on what is actually an attack
A second phase with four axes is a coverage problem more than a damage problem, which is the kind of fight where a longer Phantom Edge or a change of weapon tends to matter more than raw damage
